title: Fed holds at 3.75–4.00% with two dissents favouring a hike; 10-year UST yield above 5%
content:
The Fed left its target range unchanged at **3.75–4.00%** on 28 October in a 10–2 vote. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented in favour of a 25bp increase, a clear hawkish signal. The next FOMC meeting is on 9 December.

Treasury yields rose after the decision, with the 10-year UST trading around **5.02–5.05%** and the 2-year near 4.7%, according to CNBC and CNN. Sources differ on closing levels. US equities ended higher, with the S&P 500 and Dow up for a third straight session, though the S&P 500 was volatile intraday. With oil elevated and two voters already favouring tightening, the debate is shifting from when to cut to whether a hike is needed.

title: AI cash-burn fears trigger sharp US tech selloff; Nasdaq suffers worst day since June
content:
US equities closed sharply lower on 30 October after Amazon's third-quarter miss and Intel's weak fourth-quarter revenue guidance revived concerns over AI spending. Per Reuters, the S&P 500 fell **1.82%** to 7,580.07, the Nasdaq Composite lost **2.86%** and the Dow shed 1.09%. Intel closed down roughly 29–31% depending on the source, Amazon fell 5.6%, and Nvidia and Broadcom lost 5% and 7.3% respectively.

The Nasdaq recorded its largest one-day fall since 5 June and its worst month since March 2025, down about **5.3%** in October, while the Dow still ended the month higher. The move suggests investors are demanding returns on AI capital expenditure, a risk for index concentration in mega-cap tech.

title: Brent near $113–118/bbl after Hormuz tanker attack; oil up around 14% in October
content:
Oil rose on 30 October after a tanker was reportedly hit by explosives in the Strait of Hormuz, adding to Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure. Brent's expiring December contract settled at about **$117.64/bbl**, while the front-month January contract closed near $113.43; sources differ because of the contract roll. WTI settled near $104.

Brent gained roughly **13.6%** in October and WTI about 15%, with ship attacks reported at a record high for the month. Elevated energy prices feed inflation expectations and complicate the policy path for the Fed, which held on 28 October with two dissents for a hike. The BoJ also held at 1.25% on 30 October (8–1) but signalled further tightening, with December in play.
